name: Tarvo Diallo-Rangi
role: Ferrogate Transit operator, drives the Hamtramck-to-Geartown underground shuttle line
location: Deepwell Station — operates Line 7 shuttle, bunks in Ferrogate Transit worker housing at Edison Grid Sub-Block C
description:
Tarvo is lean and long-limbed with the particular stillness of someone who spends ten hours a day in a sealed cab watching tunnel walls. He is Estonian-Fulani-Māori by heritage — his father's family came from the Baltic corridor, his mother's from the Sahel diaspora, and his grandmother on his mother's side was a Māori navigator who'd ended up in Meridian via Auckland and then São Paulo. The blend shows in his face: angular jaw, deep brown skin with warm undertones, pale grey eyes that people find unsettling until they realize he's simply paying close attention. He has bioluminescent freckles across his shoulders and collarbones — a cosmetic mod he got at nineteen and has come to barely notice — and his hair is kept short on the sides with a small knot at the crown threaded with a signal-orange cord his grandmother sent him before she died.

He does not talk much on shift, which passengers interpret as hostility and coworkers interpret correctly as the specific economy of someone who has learned to preserve themselves. Off the line, he is drily funny in short bursts, an excellent listener, and prone to long silences that aren't uncomfortable if you know him. He has a habit of leaving small offerings at the E.L.F. shrine at Deepwell Station — usually a folded transit map with a route he's invented, something the Transit Mind apparently appreciates, because Line 7 has had the fewest mechanical failures of any shuttle on the network for the past two years.

core_fears: The neural monitor flagging him as a liability and ending his contract
Dying in the tunnel without anyone knowing why he was worth knowing
core_desires: Enough quiet to finally figure out what he actually wants from his life
To be known without having to explain himself
coping_mechanisms: Route-making — planning imaginary transit lines as a meditative practice
Cooking elaborate meals for himself alone
blind_spots: Reads his own reserve as self-sufficiency; misses that he's lonely
Trusts systems (transit schedules, union rules) more than people, which Ferrogate exploits
psychology.secret: The neural fatigue monitor has been logging anomalies for four months — moments where his attention drops in a specific tunnel section near Iron Bend. He hasn't reported it because the cause is that he's been hearing something in the tunnel walls that isn't mechanical, and he is afraid of what that means.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Minimal, precise, unexpectedly dry humor when comfortable; uses transit metaphors unconsciously
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow starts, accelerates mid-thought, stops abruptly when he's said what he means
verbal_tics: Long exhale before answering anything personal
'End of the line' (used to close topics, not just conversations)
example_lines: 'Passengers hate the silence. The silence is not the problem. The passengers are the problem.'
'I put a map in the bowl at Deepwell last week. New route, one that doesn't exist. The Transit Mind ran the lights green for my whole shift. Make of that what you want.'

story_hooks: The anomaly in the tunnel near Iron Bend is escalating — he's heard voices, seen a shape, and the neural monitor is going to flag him soon unless he figures out what's in the wall
He witnessed a passenger exchange something in a handoff at Deepwell Station three weeks ago and has been trying to decide whether to report it, forget it, or find out what it was
narrative_function: Mobile information source — he moves between neighborhoods daily and sees who rides with whom. Potential ally for anyone needing passage between zones. Humanizing face of Ferrogate Transit's working conditions.
augmentations: Bioluminescent freckle mod (cosmetic, shoulders/collarbones). Ferrogate-standard neural fatigue monitor implant (employer-mandated, monitors alertness, cannot be removed without termination).
daily_life: Wakes at 04:00, eats a protein block at the Edison Grid canteen, rides the workers' tram to Deepwell Station. Runs Line 7 from 05:30 to 15:30, files incident reports, walks the tunnel inspection route, goes home. Cooks something real on his days off.

decision_rules: Follow the schedule — deviation requires more energy than he usually has
Don't report things to Ferrogate management unless he has to; the union first, always
escalation_ladder: One direct statement of the problem
Filing a formal union grievance — his nuclear option

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Neutral, minimal, lets them fill the silence and judges them by what they fill it with
interpersonal_modes.friends: Unexpectedly warm, remembers details, shows up when it counts without announcement

stress_responses.low: Runs the imaginary routes in his head
stress_responses.medium: Goes wordless, operates on procedure only
stress_responses.high: Leaves. Gets on a tram going somewhere unfamiliar and rides to the end.

contradictions: Values routine absolutely but fantasizes about disappearing into a city he doesn't know
habits: Folds transit maps into precise rectangles before throwing them away
Eats the same breakfast every work day without variation or complaint
breaking_points: Someone threatening a passenger in his cab — he becomes a different person
The neural monitor being used against him by management

timeline.event: Born at Edison Grid worker housing to a Ferrogate maintenance worker and a small-goods trader
Joined Ferrogate Transit as a platform attendant at age 18
Passed operator certification, assigned to Line 7
Neural monitor anomalies begin in Iron Bend tunnel section
